narrative.overview:
The user-selected visual world is shadcn/ui New York with a Neutral base, Lucide icons, and Noto Sans KR by default. White content, soft gray navigation, thin boundaries, and compact typography make records and travel plans easy to scan.

The whole application shares this system: map journal, record drawer, account and preference menus, place details, visit and map dialogs, travel timetable and agenda, login, first-map setup, and offline screen. Warm notebook styling is superseded by the explicit request for a clean, organized shadcn interface.

The shared memory board is a user-approved material canvas within this neutral workspace: bright pegboard, masking tape, photographs and colored notes. Its scoped palette and paper geometry belong to this surface; navigation, dialogs and editing controls continue to use the incumbent system.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral surfaces and dark primary actions with consistent focus and disabled states.
Compact operational typography and gently curved controls.
Map-first desktop workspace and touch-friendly mobile sheets.
Persistent, independent user font and color preferences.

rules.name: The Semantic Surface Rule
rules.body: Use semantic CSS variables so color preferences apply consistently to new surfaces.

rules.name: The Preference Continuity Rule
rules.body: Keep size and hierarchy consistent when a member changes their font; do not assign a mandatory serif voice to memories.

rules.name: The Workspace Layer Rule
rules.body: Keep permanent workspace regions flat; use elevation to distinguish controls and content that float over the map.

rules.name: The Material Canvas Rule
rules.body: Keep the memory-board material palette scoped to its canvas, paper, attachments and selection affordances; surrounding controls inherit semantic workspace colors.

rules.name: The Anchored Paper Rule
rules.body: Anchor paper at the top and lift its free edge through actual geometry; settle with a damped spring and keep reduced-motion paper flat.

dos: Do inherit semantic colors and shared UI primitives across every app surface.
Do preserve independent stored font and color preferences.
Do use at least 44px mobile touch targets and 16px editable input text.
Do retain visible keyboard focus, accessible record lists, and sticky mobile save actions.
Do let the map, photographs, and existing pins carry content-specific visual interest.
donts: Don't restore warm paper surfaces, vermilion actions, notebook rules, or mandatory serif memory headings outside the explicitly approved memory-board material canvas and its local empty state.
Don't introduce a separate color, typography, or control system for travel planning.
Don't infer reusable UI colors from preserved map tiles or pin assets.
Don't obscure inline errors or dismiss a form while saving.
